Objection handling

Answer bank

Every question our leads have asked, clustered and answered - what to say, the proof behind it, what they ask next, and the trap. Domain and track variants appear at the top of an answer when the controls above change it.

Coverage - how these 28 clusters were built, and what was checked

Every lead-voiced field across all 543 call records was split into 5,421 individual statements - questions raised, concerns, coding, DSA, technical and experience doubts, skill gaps, misconceptions, objections, motivations, barriers and timeline expectations. Sales-rep-written fields were excluded. Each statement was matched against the cluster set, and the unmatched residue was re-scanned for recurring themes.

That residue pass added eight clusters the earlier 20-cluster analysis did not carry: G1 program comparison and overlap with other IK courses · G2 instructor credibility · G3 job support and referrals · G4 batch timings and recordings · G5 remote, travel and relocation · G6 product vs services vs GCC targeting · G7 whether the capstone is real · G8 being between jobs. Everything left unmatched after that was narrative rather than a question - call logistics, next-step notes and rep commentary.

Every recurring question, in one place

The eleven that keep coming up. Seven are answered in the Advisor FAQ block below with how to run the answer, the next steps in order, and an example to tell. Four were already covered and link straight to the existing cluster. Nothing here lives outside the answer bank.

  1. B1 How does my current background or role map to FDE?
  2. H1 I already work with AI, GenAI and agentic AI - what does FDE add?
  3. H2 I use AI tools but do not know LLMs, RAG, agents or evals deeply - am I ready?
  4. C1 How much Python and coding is actually required?
  5. H3 I have experience but no production AI exposure - how do I bridge it?
  6. E1 What FDE opportunities actually exist in India, at my level?
  7. G6 Which roles and companies should I target?
  8. H5 Is FDE right for my seniority, or should I stay on my current path?
  9. H4 How does FDE compare with AI Engineer, Solutions Architect or Tech Lead?
  10. H6 Is the programme worth the investment?
  11. H7 Price is the blocker - how do I stop it becoming a price-led call?

Late-stage objections - the ones that arrive after they already understand the role.

  1. J1 Self-study could achieve the same thing
  2. J2 Not the right time / just exploring / need to think
  3. J3 Will companies accept my mobile, testing or PM background?
  4. J4 Will I actually get interviews? My last course produced none
  5. J5 23 weeks is a lot / I do not have the time
Already covered, so not duplicated. “Should I go FDE or stay as tech lead?” is E4 for the track question and H4 for the path comparison. “Is FDE a bubble?” is E3, with the funded-commitment evidence and the steelmanned sceptic case in Category. “How much ROI?” is H6.
On the last two. They are answered as value and sequence, with no fee, EMI, scholarship or refund figure anywhere in this tool. Those change and must come from the current approved commercial sheet, never from memory or from here.

Category durability

Is this real, or is it hype?

The question every sceptical senior lead asks in the first five minutes. Both cases are laid out here with sources and dates. Lead with the funded commitments, then answer the objection they were actually going to raise - it is far more persuasive than pretending there isn't one.

Use both, and say why. Adjacent roles outnumber FDE-titled ones roughly three and a half to one in India. A lead who searches only “Forward Deployed Engineer” sees a fraction of their real market - and a lead who is told there are thousands of FDE roles will not find them. Show the Core FDE numbers for what the role is, and the adjacent pool for where the jobs are.

      Hiring loop

      The interview process

      Five to seven rounds depending on the company. Switch between the IC and manager loop - they are different processes, not the same one with a different title.

      Employer interview loops

      How the real loops run, company by company

      The FDE loop is not a MAANG+ loop, and this is IK's sharpest single differentiator - no competitor programme teaches the decomposition round or the client simulation. Evidence confidence is labelled on each: documented means recruiter- or candidate-confirmed; known pattern means consistently reported but not officially published.

      More than 30% of the FDE openings tracked globally are in India. The loops below are global benchmarks - Indian teams and GCCs hiring for the same role run variations of the same shape. - IK FDE Interview Cheatsheet, India edition, 2026

      Why strong engineers fail

      Ten patterns that reject otherwise-strong candidates. Most have nothing to do with whether they can code - which is exactly why generic preparation does not clear this loop.

      The question bank - 48 prompts

      Written the way an interviewer asks them. Send a lead three from their domain after the first call; it converts better than a curriculum PDF. Before solving, they should name the user, the outcome, the data, the constraints and the success metric.

      Proof of work

      The portfolio that gets them hired

      A lead is competing for a role they have not done yet. Without on-the-job FDE reps, a portfolio of things they actually built and deployed is the clearest evidence a hiring panel can see. Four projects chosen to cover the bar beat a pile of demos.

      Experienced FDEs earn about 24% above comparable customer-support engineers and about 16% above technical account managers (TeamLease Digital, via IK brochure p.4).
      Raise this before they do. What a sceptical lead will find on Google: Glassdoor all-India average ₹13.2 LPA; Bengaluru average ₹17.0 LPA, 25th–75th percentile ₹11.1–36.2 LPA. The gap is because Glassdoor pools genuine FDE roles with mistitled ones. Raise this before they do.
      All bands are advertised or employer-stated ranges, not guaranteed offers. Never quote the top of a band as the expectation. Never quote US dollar figures to an India audience - the US decks carry them and they inflate expectations badly.

      Competitive intelligence

      Who else is selling this in India

      Five programmes were already in market before ours. A lead who has done any research has seen at least one. Know the pricing, know where each is genuinely better, and never disparage an IIT brand - reframe on the job to be done.

      Read this first. Two of the four battle-card answers below only work if IK publishes verified cohort outcomes in rupees. Until that exists, do not attack a competitor's salary claims - you would be inviting the same question back.

      Claim guardrails

      Do not say this

      Everything here is something a PA could reasonably say today that the evidence does not support. Read it once before your first call and again before any webinar.

      The 11 claims to avoid, and why
      ClaimWhy not
      neverReadiness percentages from the current webinar deckEvery recomputed figure lands 5–25 points below the deck. QA/SDET is shown at 48% and computes to about 23%; TPM/PM shown at 55% computes to about 35%. Use the 100-point skill signature in this tool instead - it is traceable block by block.
      never“There are FDE manager roles in India”One manager-level posting in 133. The manager and head ladder evidence is global (Deloitte, Anthropic, Replit, Vercel). Always label it.
      neverUS dollar salary figuresThey appear throughout the US masterclass decks. Stripped from all India material deliberately. Quoting them destroys credibility on an India call.
      never“QA/SDET, Frontend, Mobile and Security are eligible” - without checkingUNRESOLVED CONFLICT: the brochure's “who fits” list (p.4) excludes all four. The webinar deck includes SDET/QA and Mobile, and the masterclass script calls Security “the strongest hand in the room”. Two published assets disagree. 44 leads across those domains. Settle this before the next webinar.
      neverFees, EMI, scholarships, refund or placement termsNot in this tool by design. Use the current approved commercial sheet.
      never“No prerequisites”AI/ML is not a prerequisite. Software-engineering fundamentals and Python proficiency are, explicitly (FAQ 02). Softening this is what produces refunds.
      careful“You'll be job-ready in 23 weeks”23 weeks to ready, plus a 3–6 week hiring loop. Two clocks.
      careful“Embedded means you relocate”It does not. Remote-first with customer standups is common; Palantir globally puts onsite at ~25%. Correct this proactively for India.
      carefulThe SDK-plus-cloud triplet as a market requirementOpenAI Agents SDK + AWS, Google ADK + Vertex, Claude Agent SDK + Azure reflects curriculum design as much as market demand. Frame as stack coverage, not as what employers ask for.
      carefulManager interview-loop specifics as established factSourced from a single US session, 11 Aug 2026. Present as indicative.
      carefulJob counts without scope and levelThe 2,326-ID broad index includes adjacent roles and is for discovery, not a claim that India has 2,326 open FDE jobs. The curated 133-role set drives FDE requirement evidence; always name the scope and pair volume with the level split.
      ⚠ The one conflict to settle before the next webinar
      Two published assets disagree about who is welcome. The brochure's “Engineers from any of these roles fit” list (p.4) does not include QA/SDET, Frontend, Mobile or Security. The webinar deck's “Who can become an FDE” slide does include SDET/QA and Mobile, and the masterclass script calls Security “the strongest hand in the room”. Until it is settled, a PA quoting one asset contradicts the other. This is a decision for the program owner, not for sales to resolve on a call.
      New since 24 Aug 2026 - eight more claims to watch
      ClaimWhy not
      never“There are thousands of FDE jobs in India”Roughly 250–270 titled roles are open at any time (TeamLease Digital via Rediff / Business Standard, Jun 2026). Global titled roles run about 500–800. The 2,326-ID index in this tool is Core plus adjacent discovery, not open FDE headcount.
      neverUS or global FDE compensation in an India conversationPalantir FDSE runs $171K–$295K with a median near $211K, and frontier-lab senior packages clear $350K–$550K (Levels.fyi, Aug 2026). Those numbers are real and completely irrelevant to an India offer. Quoting them destroys the call.
      never“₹75 LPA average” or “up to ₹1.8 Cr”Those are competitor landing-page figures (Futurense) drawn from market ceilings, not verified placements. Do not repeat a rival's unverifiable claim in order to match it.
      never“95% of AI projects fail” as a flat statementMIT Project NANDA (Jul 2025) is self-described as preliminary and not peer-reviewed, and it measures pilots with no measurable P&L impact within roughly six months. Say that, or say nothing.
      carefulReadiness percentages from the FDE Scorecard PDFReconciled, with two exceptions. Multiply a Scorecard figure by 0.89 to put it on this tool's denominator; the rest of any difference is weighting. State the exceptions plainly: the Scorecard overstates an ML Engineer's FDE-specific AI readiness, and understates DevOps, SRE and Security backgrounds because it has no security and governance dimension. See the reconciliation below.
      careful“FDE is a permanently scarce elite role”The services-trap critique is legitimate and comes from inside the category. Position the durable skill stack - discovery, integration, evals, governance - not the permanence of the job title.
      carefulInstitutional commitment figuresOpenAI's Deployment Company ($4B+), Anthropic's Ode (~$1.5B), Microsoft Frontier (~$2.5B) and AWS (~$1B) are announced commitments, not deployed spend or confirmed headcount. Label them as commitments and date them.
      carefulTravel and relocationPalantir globally puts onsite near 25%; Commure up to 50%; defence and industrial FDEs 40–75%. India patterns are more remote-first. Correct the relocation fear proactively rather than defending it later.
      Reconciling the FDE Scorecard with this tool's 100-point model
      Resolved, with two exceptions worth naming on a call. The Scorecard PDF and this tool looked like they disagreed by up to 29 points on the same question. They mostly do not. Two documented differences in method account for most of it, and what is left is a real disagreement about exactly two backgrounds - which is a far more useful thing to know than "the numbers do not match".
